{
  "jobspec": "#!/bin/bash

# Flux batch script
#
# NOTE: This workflow relies on Snakemake + DRMAA with Slurm-style options to submit many sub-jobs.
# Flux does not provide a DRMAA interface by default, and the `slurm-drmaa` module targets Slurm.
# There is no direct translation for this submission mechanism in a portable Flux script.
#
# Performance implication of omission: without a Flux-compatible executor/back-end, Snakemake will not
# dispatch cluster jobs; it may run locally within a single allocation, greatly reducing scalability.

# This is a self-submitting Flux script: run it directly (e.g., `./rc_test_snakemake.flux.sh`).
# It will submit itself to Flux with the translated *top-level* resource requests.

# Translated resources from Slurm:
#   -c 1        -> -c 1
#   -t 2-00:00  -> -t 2d
JOBID=$(flux batch -N 1 -n 1 -c 1 -t 2d --wrap "bash $0 __flux_inner")

echo "Submitted Flux job: $JOBID"

if [ "${1:-}" = "__flux_inner" ]; then
  # NOTE: Slurm -p priority not translated.
  # Performance implication: without a queue/constraint mapping, the job may run on any eligible resources; you are not forcing the priority partition.

  # NOTE: Slurm --mem 4G not translated.
  # Performance implication: without a memory reservation/limit, the job may contend for memory or be OOM-killed, affecting reliability/performance.

  # NOTE: Slurm -o/-e with %A expansion (jobid) not translated.
  # Performance implication: none; operational implication: log filenames may not be unique unless you add uniqueness.

  module unload python || true
  module load gcc conda2 slurm-drmaa/1.1.1
  conda activate rctest

  # NOTE: --drmaa argument is retained, but will only work if a DRMAA backend compatible with Flux is available (typically not).
  flux run -n 1 -c 1 snakemake \
    --snakefile src/20_62_nonallelespec_rc-test-Snakefile.py \
    --jobs 9980 \
    --restart-times 0 \
    --cluster-config config/rc-test-snakemake-cluster.json \
    --latency-wait 120 \
    --drmaa " -c {cluster.cores} -p {cluster.partition} --mem={cluster.mem} -t {cluster.time} -o {cluster.out} -e {cluster.err} -J {cluster.J}"

  conda deactivate
fi
"
}
